title: "Pretraining"
description: "The initial training of a model on a broad dataset before task-specific adaptation or evaluation."
term: "Pretraining"
letter: "P"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Pretraining gives a model broad capabilities by learning from a large
collection of data before it is adapted for a particular use. It is similar
to building general knowledge before taking specialized instruction.

## Technical explanation

Pretraining optimizes a model objective over a broad corpus. Language models
often learn to predict masked or next tokens; other model families use
objectives such as contrastive learning or reconstruction. The learned
weights are later reused as a starting point for downstream tasks.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Pretraining can produce reusable representations and reduce the labeled data
needed for later adaptation. It is also resource-intensive and carries
important choices about data provenance, filtering, licensing, privacy, and
evaluation.

## How it works

Training examples are constructed from the corpus and passed through the
model. A self-supervised objective supplies learning targets from the data
itself, and optimization updates model parameters over many batches. The
resulting checkpoint may then be fine-tuned, aligned, or used directly.

## Practical example

A decoder-only language model is pretrained on text using next-token
prediction. Afterward, a separate fine-tuning stage can teach it to follow
instructions, with evaluation determining whether it performs the intended
tasks reliably.

## Common misconceptions

- Pretraining data is not automatically clean, unbiased, or suitable for
  every downstream use.
- Pretraining and fine-tuning are different stages, even when both use
  gradient-based training.
